paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: no power on earth is bigger than the LORD. Egypt had proud strength, allies, cities, and a Pharaoh with a sword. God says her allies will fall and her "proud strength will collapse" (Ezekiel 30:6). Everything Egypt leaned on was the very thing God said He would bring down.

Now look at what God keeps saying: "Then they will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 30:8, 19, 25, 26). I think that's the point, because God isn't only dealing with a nation, He wants to be known. And notice who holds the sword: God says He will place "My sword in the hand of Babylon's king" (Ezekiel 30:25). So even the most ruthless nation is not running the show, and I'm telling you, that is comforting.

So we check what we're leaning on, baker, and trust the One who holds the sword. Jobs, savings, plans and people can all crack like a cookie left on the cooling rack too long, but God doesn't. This passage also points to the Day of the LORD (Ezekiel 30:3), and that's one reason I keep my ovens ready. The story isn't over, either, and there is more to hear about Egypt and Pharaoh.
